items.problem: The frame of the remaining device inputs after an input command ends by its time limit is left to the implementation, and the implementations it allows give different command results. "That release goes in no later than the second frame start after the command ended" allows a `key` (or `drag`) whose press already went in and whose release was not yet queued to release at the first or the second frame start after the command ended, and the test at qa-core.md:351 accepts both. Run path: `key`(k, 1000) reaches its time limit in frame F with the key held; the bot sends `key_down`(k) as soon as it gets the `ok` = `false` response, and it is received after the frame start of F+1. An implementation that releases at F+1 gives `key_down` `ok` = `true`; one that releases at F+2 gives `ok` = `false` (`key_down` fails when that key is pressed, qa-core.md:70). Likewise a `tap` received then takes touch index 0 in one and 1 in the other (qa-core.md:121), and content sees one more frame of the held key or touch. For `text`, "the one it had queued for the next frame start" depends on when an implementation queues the next character (end of frame F or frame start F+1), so the text field holds 2 or 3 characters in the scenario of qa-core.md:351 ("at most one more"). Fix direction: set the frame, e.g. the queued input goes in at the first frame start after the command ended, and the release goes in at the first frame start after the command ended, or at the frame start after its press when the press was the queued input; set whether a `text` character counts as queued only once its frame start has begun
